applicable_algorithms.formula: let r = surface_water.recurrence; if r is Absence -> 'none'; else if r >= 75 -> 'perennial'; else if r >= 25 -> 'seasonal'; else if r >= 1 -> 'occasional'; else -> 'never'
let n = indices.ndvi; if n < 0 -> 'water_or_snow'; else if n < 0.1 -> 'bare'; else if n < 0.3 -> 'sparse'; else if n < 0.5 -> 'moderate'; else -> 'dense'

let n = clamp(indices.ndvi, 0.40, 0.85); AGB_Mg_ha = 505 * pow(n, 2.04)  // Baccini et al. 2008 (Environ Res Lett 3:045011), pan-tropical Africa fit, n=263 inventory plots paired with MODIS NDVI 463 m, R² = 0.82, RMSE 50.5 Mg/ha. Outside NDVI ∈ [0.40, 0.85] return Absence{reason:'outside_calibration_envelope'}.
fraction_green = (1/N_ring) * count_{c in K3_ring} { indices.ndvi(c) >= 0.4 }; access_score = clamp01(fraction_green / 0.20)

is_mountain = (elevation >= 2500) OR (elevation >= 1500 AND local_slope >= 2 deg) OR (elevation >= 1000 AND local_slope >= 5 deg) OR (elevation >= 300 AND local_relief_7km > 300); kapos_class follows; is_green = indices.ndvi >= 0.30; MGCI = (sum_polygon(is_mountain AND is_green) / sum_polygon(is_mountain)) * 100

band_metadata.description: Copernicus GLO-30 DEM statistics at the cell: elevation mean, percentiles, slope, aspect (sin/cos), TRI roughness.
band_metadata.interpretation: Default DEM source for emem — superior to SRTM at high latitudes and over dense canopy. Use for hydro-routing, viewshed, slope-stability, and sea-level-rise exposure.
band_metadata.pitfalls: GLO-30 is a *surface* model (DSM): it includes building / canopy heights. Subtract `landcover.tree` × typical canopy height for a bare-earth approximation, or pull GLO-90 for a DTM-like product.

band_metadata.description: Tessera annual foundation embedding (128-D, stored upstream as int8 + per-pixel f32 scale; recall decodes to f32 for cosine scoring). A learned multimodal vector that fuses Sentinel-2 optical, Sentinel-1 radar, and seasonality into one position-stable vector per cell per year. The default similarity surface for `/v1/find_similar` because it captures land-cover, structure, and recent change in one shot.
band_metadata.interpretation: Compare via cosine similarity (or Hamming on the `geotessera.bin128` sign-bit sibling). Two cells with similarity > 0.85 are usually the same physical archetype (e.g. dense urban, mature mangrove, sparse savanna). Not directly interpretable per dimension — treat as opaque.
band_metadata.pitfalls: Yearly cadence: a cell that flips from forest to clearing mid-year reads as the *annual mean* until the next vintage. Use `temporal_diff` or `phenology` to detect intra-year change.

provenance.caution: model output: a learned representation, not a measurement. Subject to training bias, domain shift, and encoder revision; treat as a hypothesis and corroborate against a deterministic band before load-bearing use.
provenance.tamper_evidence_note: this band's class declares signed_model_checkpoint, but THIS fact carries no checkpoint hash: it came from an upstream product rather than an encoder this responder ran. You are trusting the signer and the cited source, which is what attester_only means. Facts signed by an encoder this responder ran carry the checkpoint hash inside sources[].id, and keep the stronger claim.

band_metadata.description: Three optical-index scalars derived from Sentinel-2 L2A: NDVI, NDRE, NDMI. The most-pulled vegetation surface — these are what algorithms like `flood_risk@2`, `crop_stress@1`, and `irrigation_demand@1` compose.
band_metadata.interpretation: NDVI < 0 = water / snow; 0 – 0.2 = bare soil / urban; 0.2 – 0.5 = sparse / stressed vegetation; 0.5 – 0.8 = healthy crops / shrub; > 0.8 = dense closed canopy. NDMI tracks canopy water content (negative = dry, positive = moist). NDRE is more sensitive to chlorophyll than NDVI and saturates later — preferred for in-season nitrogen monitoring.
band_metadata.pitfalls: Read `surface_class` on the fact before the value. It carries the per-pixel Sentinel-2 SCL class the responder actually probed at this cell (`scl`, `label`, `vegetation_valid`) and answers a question `confidence` does not: confidence scores radiometric cleanliness, so a snow-covered field in January is a clean pixel and scores 0.95 while the NDVI on it measures snow, not vegetation. `vegetation_valid: false` (snow, water, shadow) means the number is real but is not a vegetation reading. Prefer this over the scene-level `weather.cloud_cover` / `cloud_pct` proxies: those describe the whole scene, `surface_class` describes this pixel. Absent when the SCL band could not be read, in which case confidence falls back to scene-level cloud cover and the scene-level proxies are all there is. NDVI saturates above ~0.85 (use NDRE / `geotessera` for dense canopies).
band_metadata.references: Tucker 1979 (NDVI); Gitelson & Merzlyak 1994 (NDRE); Gao 1996 (NDMI / NDWI); Xu 2006 (MNDWI = (B03-B11)/(B03+B11)); Key & Benson 2006 (NBR = (B08-B12)/(B08+B12)); Hall et al. 1995 (NDSI = (B03-B11)/(B03+B11)); Zha et al. 2003 (NDBI = (B11-B08)/(B11+B08)); Rikimaru et al. 2002 (BSI = ((B11+B04)-(B08+B02))/((B11+B04)+(B08+B02))); Hardisky et al. 1983 (NDWI_Gao = (B03-B08)/(B03+B08), the leaf-water-content form used by the algal-bloom water gate)

band_metadata.description: Annual nightlight composite at the cell (DMSP-OLS V4 intercalibrated stable lights, 1992-2013). VIIRS DNB v22 was the originally-targeted source but EOG/CSM moved its archive behind OAuth in 2024-2025; the wired open-data path is NOAA NCEI NGDC, the only globally-mirrored, anonymous, Range-readable annual nightlight time series.
band_metadata.interpretation: Strong proxy for human activity intensity at night — picks up settlements down to ~hamlet scale. A drop year-over-year often signals out-migration, conflict, or grid failure; a spike signals new development. Comparing DMSP-OLS DN to VIIRS DNB radiance requires the Li & Zhou 2017 (Remote Sensing 9:637) intercalibration regression — DN is not the same physical unit as nW · cm⁻² · sr⁻¹.
band_metadata.pitfalls: Snow on roofs reflects moonlight and inflates DN in winter at high latitudes. The intercalibration mask zeroes ephemeral lights (fires, gas flares); a 0 at this cell genuinely means 'no measurable persistent night-time emission' and IS a Primary fact (not Absence). Privacy: aggregate_only at min_res 11; finer recall is denied. Coverage: -65°S to 75°N (DMSP-OLS V4 raster bounds).
band_metadata.references: Elvidge et al. 1997 (DMSP-OLS); Li & Zhou 2017 (Remote Sensing 9:637, DN-to-radiance regression)

band_metadata.description: IBM-NASA Prithvi-EO-2.0-300M-TL per-cell foundation embedding. The cell's 6-band 224×224 Sentinel-2 L2A chip (Blue/Green/Red/Narrow-NIR/SWIR1/SWIR2 in HLS V2 order, ~30 m equivalent) is encoded by the Vision Transformer; the materializer signs the encoder's last-block CLS token (1024-D, post-norm) as the fact value alongside the temporal-encoder's year + DOY embeddings. The cube slot allocates 384 dims at offset 894 as the layout reservation; fact `value` carries the full 1024-D vector and downstream similarity (find_similar) reads that directly.
band_metadata.interpretation: Compare via cosine similarity. Two cells with cosine > 0.85 share a structural archetype at the 6.7 km × 6.7 km Prithvi receptive-field scale (urban core, tropical forest, irrigated cropland, mangrove, etc.). Scene-aware and date-aware: the temporal encoder shifts the embedding with year + DOY, so two vintages of the same cell are deliberately distinct.
band_metadata.pitfalls: Receptive field is 6720 m × 6720 m at 30 m pixel pitch — the embedding represents a chip centred on the cell, not the 9.55 m cell footprint. Two cell64s within the same chip extent share most of their Prithvi vector. For per-cell discrimination at 10 m use `geotessera`. Privacy class is `l2_only_with_model_cid` because the embedding can leak chip content; every fact carries the model checkpoint hash so agents can verify the encoder version.

provenance.caution: model output: a learned representation, not a measurement. Subject to training bias, domain shift, and encoder revision; treat as a hypothesis and corroborate against a deterministic band before load-bearing use.

band_metadata.references: https://huggingface.co/ibm-nasa-geospatial/Prithvi-EO-2.0-300M-TL ; Jakubik, J. et al. 2023. Foundation Models for Generalist Geospatial Artificial Intelligence (Prithvi). arXiv:2310.18660

honesty_warnings: frozen_pretrained_encoder: this is a per-cell forward pass through the frozen Prithvi-EO-2.0-300M-TL encoder (no fine-tuning at this responder). The embedding captures whatever HLS V2 pretraining captured; quality for any downstream task depends on how well that task aligns with masked-autoencoder objectives.

band_metadata.description: Sentinel-1 RTC (Radiometrically Terrain Corrected) C-band SAR backscatter in dB. Two slots (VV, VH) but only VV is currently materialized.
band_metadata.interpretation: Higher values = more backscatter = rougher / wetter / more vertical-structured surface. Smooth water sits near −20 dB; bare soil −12 to −8; forest canopy −10 to −6; urban can exceed 0. Works at night and through cloud — the all-weather complement to `indices.ndvi`.
band_metadata.pitfalls: VH slot is reserved but currently unattested. Treat sentinel1_raw as a 1-vector (VV-only) when no VH-bearing attestation is present at the cell. Speckle noise is significant — average a 3×3 cell window before drawing inference.

band_metadata.pitfalls: VH slot is reserved but currently unattested. Treat sentinel1_raw as a 1-vector (VV-only) when no VH-bearing attestation is present at the cell. Speckle noise is significant — average a 3×3 cell window before drawing inference.

band_metadata.description: JRC Global Surface Water v1.4 features at 30 m: recurrence, occurrence, seasonality, transitions (1984–2021 climatology) plus current-year occurrence updates.
band_metadata.interpretation: `recurrence` is the canonical signed answer to 'has this cell historically been wet?' — 0 = never water, 100 = water every year of the record. `occurrence` adds current-year updates. Use for flood-baseline reasoning, not real-time inundation (for that use Sentinel-1 + radar water).
band_metadata.pitfalls: Bounded ±60° latitude (JRC's observation footprint). Polar regions return Absence. Glacier and turbid-river cells can score high recurrence without being navigable open water.

band_metadata.description: Compact current-weather quad sourced from Open-Meteo / MET Norway forecast blends. Four scalars covering temperature, cloud, precipitation, and wind.
band_metadata.dimension_description: Air temperature at 2 m above ground.
band_metadata.interpretation: Current-state climate the agent can fold into algorithms like `heat_index@1` or `evapotranspiration_fao56@1`. For climatology / historical fields use `terraclimate` or `koppen`.
band_metadata.pitfalls: Tempo is `medium` because forecasts are refreshed hourly; recall for old tslots returns the historical reanalysis if the upstream supports it, otherwise Absence.

spatial_basis.computed_from: the cell's own latitude, not a stored constant
spatial_basis.must_not_do: difference two adjacent cells and read the result as a gradient. Source pixels are metres across and so are cells, so neighbouring cells can be samples of the same pixel, and the difference would be a pixel with itself.
spatial_basis.per_band_resolution: not stated: this responder has no band-to-source mapping, and an invented resolution that looked measured would be worse than its absence. See `sources` on each fact for the scheme that produced it.
spatial_basis.what_a_value_is: a sample of the source pixel overlapping this cell, not an average over the cell. The cell is an ADDRESS; the pixel is the measurement.
